title: Christoffer Sehested (Danish envoy in Vienna) → Frederik III and chancellor Christen Thomesen Sehested: wholly enciphered relations
correspondents: Christoffer Sehested → Frederik III of Denmark; Christoffer Sehested → Christen Thomesen Sehested
shelfmark: Rigsarkivet (Copenhagen), Tyske Kancelli, Udenrigske Afdeling (TKUA), Speciel del, Kejseren: Gesandtskabsrelationer med bilag, pakke 1630-58, læg "Relationer fra Christoffer Sehested 1657" (cited by Fridericia as Østrig 46)
folio_note: Arkivalieronline unit 260651 (434 images, microfilm scans), images 108 to about 170: some 40 pages of cipher (letters dated 17/1, 10/2?, 14/2, 7-17/2, March 1657 ...). Seen at full size: image 126 (14 Feb 1657, 'Sire', 24 lines).
status: Viewed 11 Nov 2026. The letters are written entirely in a number cipher: one- and two-digit numbers divided by colons, a t-shaped word divider, and nomenclator signs (Σ, Ψ, GG, XX, X, H, ♀, Ω, 7000, mm). No decipherment is written on the cipher leaves. Loose slips in a 19th-century hand (images 124, 125, 137, 138) carry a German decipherment of the letter to Chr. Thomesen Sehested of 7/17 Feb 1657 and its postscript, with the nomenclator signs left unresolved; older-hand plaintext leaves stand at images 112-115 and 157-158. Fridericia, Adelsvældens sidste Dage (1894), note 62 to p. 242, cites the letters and thanks Dr E. Gigas for 'a decipherment of Sehested's letters': so the letters were deciphered in the 1880s, but no text of the decipherment is printed and the slips in the volume cover only part. Not on DECODE (search 'Sehested': 0).
why: Denmark's secret alliance talks with the Emperor on the eve of the 1657 war with Sweden; the plaintext has never been printed, and the code signs for persons are unresolved even on the archivist's slips.
score_note: Scored from the scans during the 11 Nov 2026 Nordic sweep (research/sweep_2026-11-11_nordic/); image 126 read at full size, images 101-170 on thumbnails
verify: Not vetted as open: Gigas's decipherment (used by Fridericia 1894, and Gigas, Grev Bernardino de Rebolledo, 1883, pp. 283 f.) is prior art of unknown extent. Match each decipherment slip to its letter, list the letters with no plaintext in the volume, and ask Rigsarkivet whether Gigas's full decipherment survives. The archive also holds 'Christoffer Sehested keys 1650-70' (Daisy heid 1449582, see research/scandinavia).
prior_art: partly read: E. Gigas deciphered Sehested's letters for Fridericia (Adelsvældens sidste Dage, 1894, note 62; archive.org full text opened 11 Nov 2026); slips with part of it lie in the volume. No printed plaintext found; DECODE search 'Sehested', 'Wien 1657': no record of it; not in Tomokiyo's unsolved.htm
access_note: free on Arkivalieronline, no login; images also at api.rigsarkivet.dk/ao/v1/images/<id> (ao.py)

title: Bonifacio Ruggieri and Alfonso Rossetto (Este envoys in Rome) → Ercole II d'Este: letter on Bologna and Ferrara, the last third in cipher
correspondents: Bonifacio Ruggieri and Alfonso Rossetto → Ercole II d'Este, Duke of Ferrara
shelfmark: Uppsala universitetsbibliotek, Waller collection, Waller Ms it-01133
folio_note: 2 leaves (292 x 211 mm), 3 images: f. 1r has 18 lines of clear text then 10 lines of cipher; f. 1v opens with 4 more cipher lines, then the close and both signatures; f. 2v the address. About 14 lines, perhaps 550-650 signs.
status: Viewed 11 Nov 2026 (the three TIFFs, read at 1,000 px a page). Alvin record 192068: 'Matters concerning the relations between Bologna and Ferrara, partly written in cipher.' The cipher is a set of letter-like signs and letters with diacritics (b, d, x, y, t, l with strokes and loops), written continuously; nothing is written between the lines or in the margin, and no decipherment sheet is among the images. Dealer's stamp of Damiano Muoni: a stray from the Este envoys' correspondence, whose main run is in Modena. Not on DECODE.
why: Ferrara's envoys at the court of Paul III on the Bologna-Ferrara dispute; the clear part sets the subject, the cipher holds what they would not write openly.
score_note: Scored from the scans during the 11 Nov 2026 Nordic sweep (research/sweep_2026-11-11_nordic/); all three images viewed

title: "Kloge Søren" (Søren Christensen): his Cyprianus, a book of charms and cures written almost wholly in a symbol cipher
correspondents: Søren Christensen, "Kloge Søren" (1843-1925), cunning man, writer and owner
shelfmark: Det Kgl. Bibliotek (Copenhagen), Dansk Folkemindesamling, DFS 1997/020 (Kloge Sørens samling, from Petra Mosegaard)
folio_note: 90 leaves in one octavo volume, 109 images online; about 85 written pages of roughly 12 lines, most of it cipher in red ink; six loose slips of formulas in a second, angular sign alphabet
status: Viewed 11 Nov 2026 (contact sheet of 12 openings across the book; opening 12-13 at 1,700 px). Running text in a sign alphabet of strokes, dots, hooks and bars, with no word spaces; headings partly in clear Danish ('for Kjertelsyge', 'mod Troldom hos Fjeder-Kræet', 'at faae een Tyv til at hensvinde som Duk for Solen', 'mod Hexerie og Forgjörelse hos Mennesker og Dyr', 'For Svindsot'), a SATOR square on p. 58. No key and no decipherment on the leaves or in the record. The library's description: 'Størstedelen i lønskrift' (most of it in secret writing). Not on DECODE.
why: A complete working handbook of a 19th-century Danish cunning man, with the cures hidden in his own cipher; the clear headings give the subject of every section.
score_note: Scored from the scans during the 11 Nov 2026 Nordic sweep (research/sweep_2026-11-11_nordic/); 13 openings viewed
